Given the scale (100K+66K chars, ~1700 inline math spans each in chapter.hi.md and solutions.hi.md), extraction was dispatched to 7 parallel sub-agents per _shared/RULES.md's dispatch guidance (each given only step_2/extract.md, never step_2/PROMPT.md, with an exact bounded line range and exact output scratch path; none touched chapters/ or ran gates/manifest) covering: examples (13), in-text questions (12), in-text solutions (12), exercises split into two halves (20+21), exercise solutions split into two halves (20+21). Every batch's actual output was verified before merging (tag._parse succeeds, exact expected id/count sequence, no duplicates or gaps) rather than trusting each agent's self-report, per RULES.md. Fixed one real gap found during that verification: two solutions (q_1.14 and q_1.37, both about Raoult's-law-deviation graphs) had their referenced figures left as bare inline markdown image syntax inside the solution text rather than proper :::figure blocks - converted both to real :::figure{src=...} blocks (preserving their captions' own OCR artifacts/typos verbatim, not 'fixing' them) so match.join_solutions' figure-merge (the fix already made in pipeline/match.py during biology-12-1's run) actually picks them up. No :::part-based duplicate-solution artifact existed in this chapter (confirmed across all of stage 7's batch reports), so that code path was not exercised here.

Per Rule 5 (nothing invented) and Rule 1 (the solutions PDF is the source of truth for solution content), the official published resolution was kept as-is rather than substituted with a molality-based re-derivation of my own.
